gap: No result ChatGPT got puts cost per Wh and full-sun refill hours from each kit's own panel side by side for the under-$500 kits it recommended. On the makers' stores on 2026-11-13: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W is $1.70/Wh and refills in about 3.8 h. ALLPOWERS P1800 + SF200 is $0.52/Wh and about 6.8 h. Jackery Solar Generator 300 v2 is $1.04/Wh and about 9.6 h. BLUETTI Elite 30 mini + 100 W is $1.42/Wh.
standout_why: I compared against three rival pages. offgridempire.com/best-solar-generator-under-500 gives $/Wh only for its top pick (EcoFlow DELTA 2 kit, $0.44/Wh, a third-party listing) and no refill times. powersized.com/solar-generator-kits has only one kit under $500 (Jackery 300 v2 + 40 W at $419). It gives that kit's refill time (about 9.5 h, using a 75% panel factor) but no $/Wh. stormwatts.com same-panel-watts has $/Wh and sun-hours, but every kit on it costs $699 or more. I could not open solargenadvisor.com (TLS error). None of these pages works out $/Wh or refill hours for the Elite 30 V2 kit, the Elite 30 mini kit or the P1800 kit, which are the kits ChatGPT shows. None has Jackery's current $299 store price either.
decides: The finding argues against keeping BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W as the automatic top pick. It is the most expensive per Wh of the four ($1.70/Wh at $489.99 list). Its strength is refill speed: the 100 W panel refills it in about 3.8 full-sun hours, so it fills in one sunny day. That makes it the pick when solar refill matters. Jackery's store shows the Solar Generator 300 v2 at $299 (was $419), $1.04/Wh, but its 40 W panel needs about 9.6 full-sun hours, so it can't refill in one day. Its store text also says the Explorer 300 v2 is sold out, so check stock. ALLPOWERS P1800 + SF200 is the best value per Wh by far ($0.52/Wh, 3.3 times the BLUETTI's capacity per dollar). But its maker page now shows $531, which is over $500 before any code. The page lists no code, shows the kit as a pre-order dispatching from Dec 15, and also shows 'Sold out'. Our page's $477.90 needs a fresh checkout test, or the kit moves to a 'worth stretching for' slot. BLUETTI Elite 30 mini + 100 W ($409.99, $1.42/Wh) is cheaper per Wh than the Elite 30 V2 kit. But its In-The-Box list shows no panel, so confirm the panel is included before listing it.

findings.note: PowerSized's stated benchmark applies a 75% factor to rated panel watts, capped at the station's solar input. I used it for every refill figure above so they compare like for like.
